data.title: Staged Accident Claim Correlation — Shared Professional Enabler Network Detection
data.description: Detects potential organized crash-for-cash insurance fraud rings by identifying claims from multiple ostensibly unrelated accidents that share common professional enablers (same medical provider, legal representative, or repair shop). Organized insurance fraud rings rely on networks of corrupt professionals who process claims across multiple staged incidents. The shared professional enabler network is the most durable and detectable element of the ring, as replacing trusted corrupt professionals is harder than recruiting new participants.

| eval claim_date_epoch=strptime(claim_date, "%Y-%m-%d")

  BY medical_provider
| where accident_count >= 3
| rename medical_provider AS shared_provider
| eval provider_type="medical"
| append [
  search index=flame_insurance sourcetype=flame:claims claim_type="vehicle_accident"
  | where strptime(claim_date, "%Y-%m-%d") > relative_time(now(), "-365d")
  | stats dc(accident_id) AS accident_count,
          dc(claim_id) AS claim_count,
          values(accident_id) AS accidents,
          sum(claim_amount) AS total_claimed
    BY legal_representative
  | where accident_count >= 3
  | rename legal_representative AS shared_provider
  | eval provider_type="legal"
]
| append [
  search index=flame_insurance sourcetype=flame:claims claim_type="vehicle_accident"
  | where strptime(claim_date, "%Y-%m-%d") > relative_time(now(), "-365d")
  | stats dc(accident_id) AS accident_count,
          dc(claim_id) AS claim_count,
          values(accident_id) AS accidents,
          sum(claim_amount) AS total_claimed
    BY repair_shop
  | where accident_count >= 3
  | rename repair_shop AS shared_provider
  | eval provider_type="repair"
]
| sort - accident_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Staged Accident Claim Correlation
-- Identifies shared professional enablers across unrelated accidents
SELECT
    'medical' AS provider_type,
    a.medical_provider AS shared_provider,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) AS accident_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.claim_id) AS claim_count,
    SUM(a.claim_amount) AS total_claimed
FROM insurance_claims a
WHERE a.claim_type = 'vehicle_accident'
  AND a.claim_date >= DATEADD(year, -1, GETDATE())
  AND a.medical_provider IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.medical_provider
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) >= 3

UNION ALL

SELECT
    'legal' AS provider_type,
    a.legal_representative AS shared_provider,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) AS accident_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.claim_id) AS claim_count,
    SUM(a.claim_amount) AS total_claimed
FROM insurance_claims a
WHERE a.claim_type = 'vehicle_accident'
  AND a.claim_date >= DATEADD(year, -1, GETDATE())
  AND a.legal_representative IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.legal_representative
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) >= 3

UNION ALL

SELECT
    'repair' AS provider_type,
    a.repair_shop AS shared_provider,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) AS accident_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.claim_id) AS claim_count,
    SUM(a.claim_amount) AS total_claimed
FROM insurance_claims a
WHERE a.claim_type = 'vehicle_accident'
  AND a.claim_date >= DATEADD(year, -1, GETDATE())
  AND a.repair_shop IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.repair_shop
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) >= 3

ORDER BY accident_count DESC

references: UNODC, Organized Fraud — Issue Paper (Vienna, 2024) — Chapter II, Crash-for-Cash Fraud
UK Insurance Fraud Bureau — crash-for-cash ring intelligence
falsepositives: Legitimate high-volume medical providers or repair shops in areas with high accident rates
Law firms specializing in personal injury claims handling multiple genuine cases
Preferred provider networks directed by insurance companies
